pr_title: Make `GridPlacement`'s fields non-zero and add accessor functions.
pr_body:
# Objective

* There is no way to read the fields of `GridPlacement` once set. 
* Values of `0` for `GridPlacement`'s fields are invalid but can be set.
* A non-zero representation would be half the size.

fixes #9474

## Solution
* Add `get_start`, `get_end` and `get_span` accessor methods.
* Change`GridPlacement`'s constructor functions to panic on arguments of zero.
* Use non-zero types instead of primitives for `GridPlacement`'s fields.

---

## Changelog

`bevy_ui::ui_node::GridPlacement`:
* Field types have been changed to `Option<NonZeroI16>` and `Option<NonZeroU16>`. This is because zero values are not valid for `GridPlacement`. Previously, Taffy interpreted these as auto variants.
* Constructor functions for `GridPlacement` panic on arguments of `0`.
* Added accessor functions: `get_start`, `get_end`, and `get_span`. These return the inner primitive value (if present) of the respective fields.

## Migration Guide
`GridPlacement`'s constructor functions no longer accept values of `0`. Given any argument of `0` they will panic with a `GridPlacementError`.

issue_context.title: GridPlacement fields cannot be accessed out of crate
issue_context.body:
## What problem does this solve or what need does it fill?

I'm writing code that serializes style properties in CSS syntax. Unfortunately, the GridPlacement fields are private, and cannot be accessed out of crate.

## What solution would you like?

Allow some means to get access to the `start`, `span`, and `end` fields.

## What alternative(s) have you considered?

Although GridPlacement does support Serialize & Deserialize, this does not allow it to be serialized in the way I'd like, specifically the way grid placement is represented in CSS.
comments: Is it safe to just make these `pub`? If not, can we add read-only accessors for them?

There shouldn't be any problems with them being pub I think. There are rules for resolving conflicts like start > end etc, there aren't any invalid states.

Maybe the interface would be better expressed as an enum though?
Values of zero are ignored, so changing the fields to `Option<NonZeroI16>` with accessor functions might also be an idea.

It really depends on how pedantic you want to be. According to the [CSS standard](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/grid-row) (which is what this property is derived from even though it's not technically CSS), it's only meaningful to fill in two of the three values - start + end, start + span, or span + end.

That being said, enforcing that the data conforms to this constraint is somewhat complex, and hardly necessary; neither the code that uses these values, nor the serializer, is likely to be confused if all three values are filled in, it will just fall back to some sensible default by ignoring one of them.

What I'm working on is a framework for building Bevy UIs from XML, and that includes representing style properties in a form which is similar to what various popular CSS-in-JS packages implement: not JSON or RON, but text that looks a lot like a CSS grid expression in a stylesheet, e.g. "1 / 3". So all I really need is the ability to read the properties by whatever means you find acceptable.

(I did in fact forget about the non-zero constraint, and I'm glad you reminded me of this, so there may be some value there - CSS columns indices are 1-based, although negative numbers are also allowed.)
I implemented the non-zero with accessors approach. It seems like a reasonable change.

review_comments: If this can panic, can you add a `# Panics` section to these docs now?
Ditto elsewhere with these same changes.
